newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH EMU OPPONENTS ORGANISE, DEMAND REFERENDUM.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH EMU OPPONENTS ORGANISE, DEMAND REFERENDUM.

text.p: Finnish opponents of Economic and Monetary Union established a citizens' committee over the weekend to demand a referendum on Finnish membership of EMU, the organisers told a news conference on Monday.

"On Saturday a broad citizens' committee was established ... to safeguard democracy and demand a referendum on EMU and on the (European Union's) intergovernmental conference (IGC)," anti-EU activist Ulla Klotzer said.
"Both ... EMU and the Maastrict II treaty being born of the IGC will in an irreversible manner accelerate the formation of the EU into a real federal state," the committee said.

"The talk about joining the third stage of EMU even by a simple majority in parliament clearly show the indifference with which the political elite brushes aside the views of the majority of the people," it said in a statement.

"The majority of Finns are against EMU," Klotzer said, referring to a February poll in which 40 percent of Finns said Finland should not join EMU among the first while 21 percent said Finland should join.
